title: RentGuard Renters Policy — Late Fee Timing and Courtesy Fee Waivers
content:
Desk guidance for the premium account of a RentGuard Renters Policy: when a late fee may be charged on an installment, and when a late fee or returned-payment fee may be waived as a courtesy.

## When a late fee may be charged

A late fee is charged only when the installment is still unpaid after the late-fee grace period that starts on the installment due date.

- **Counting.** The grace period is counted in calendar days from the installment due date recorded on the billing entry, using the tier's late-fee grace period. The late fee may be posted from the day after the due date plus the grace period; on the last day of the grace period it may not yet be posted.
- **Still unpaid.** An installment is still unpaid when the amount due on that day still includes any part of it, payments having been applied oldest charge first. The amount due on a day is the sum of the installments billed with a due date on or before that day, plus the fees charged, payments returned, additional premium and refunds posted on or before it, less the payments received, fees waived, return premium and write-offs posted on or before it, and never below 0.00.
- **Once per installment.** A late fee is charged at most once per installment.
- The judgement rests on the premium account records of that installment — its term and installment number — not on the customer's account of when they paid.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, grace period of 10 calendar days).** An installment due on 5 March has a grace period running through 15 March. On 15 March no late fee may be posted; from 16 March a late fee may be posted if the installment is still unpaid that day. If a payment posted on 14 March cleared the whole of it, no late fee is charged.

## Retired clause

This clause is no longer in force: "The returned-payment fee is charged once per returned payment, referencing that return, and the reinstatement fee once per reinstatement; a fee whose tier amount is 0.00 is not charged at all." This clause has been withdrawn and superseded by the current basis for late charges on RentGuard installments.

## Courtesy waivers

- On the named insured's request, a late fee or a returned-payment fee may be waived as a courtesy.
- A courtesy waiver is granted only while the policy's waivers in the rolling 12 months are fewer than the tier's courtesy waiver allowance. The rolling 12 months end on the waiver date: a waiver counts when it was posted later than the waiver date less 12 calendar months and on or before the waiver date. The count is taken from the policy's premium account.
- A fee that has already been waived is never waived again.
- Installment fees and reinstatement fees are never waived.
- A waiver removes the full amount of the one fee entry it references.

| Fee requested for waiver | Waivers already posted in the rolling 12 months | Already waived | Waiver may be granted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Late fee or returned-payment fee | fewer than the tier allowance | no | yes |
| Late fee or returned-payment fee | equal to the tier allowance | — | no |
| Late fee or returned-payment fee | — | yes | no |
| Installment fee or reinstatement fee | — | — | no |

**Hypothetical example.** On a tier whose allowance is 1, a policy whose only earlier waiver was posted 13 months before today may receive a waiver today; one whose earlier waiver was posted 11 months ago may not.

superseded_clauses: The returned-payment fee is charged once per returned payment, referencing that return, and the reinstatement fee once per reinstatement; a fee whose tier amount is 0.00 is not charged at all.
